=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves attached at a single node, clearly visible in close-up images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, forming a rosette-like cluster)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single, undivided blade)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without any teeth or lobes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (long and narrow with a pointed tip and broader base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a long, narrow point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base, wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with lateral veins branching off at angles)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are distinct and run parallel to each other, perpendicular to the midrib)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, leaf blade appears to arise directly from stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly woody, typical of young tree seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green to reddish-brown (stem is green at the top, transitioning to reddish-brown lower down)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth, no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base; not applicable as leaves are simple and not in Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)

F. Notes: Some leaves show small holes and margin damage, likely due to physical disturbance or minor feeding, but no clear signs of pathogen or insect activity. The seedling is low-growing, emerging from leaf litter, with a rosette of leaves at the apex. Multiple images confirm consistent morphology across views.
